newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end slightly higher.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index inched higher on Thursday, the first day of trading after the National Day holiday, thanks to speculative buying of a number of Shenzhen-based counters, analysts said.
The B share index inched up 0.25 point, or 0.28 percent, to close at 89.82 on turnover of HK$23.46 million, compared with last Friday's HK$14.86 million.
Shenzhen-based property concern China Vanke became the day's star on speculative buying, analysts said. The counter rose HK$0.16, or 3.9 8 percent, to HK$4.18 on light volume of 25,100 shares.
Shenzhen Zhonghao followed with an advance of HK$0.06, or 3.87 percent, to HK$1.61 after only 5,800 shares changed hands. Building materials producer Shenzhen Fangda climbed HK$0.14 to HK$4.75.
China Marine edged up HK$0.02 to HK$6.00, with 444,800 shares traded. The advance was linked to investor confidence in the Shenzhen-based company's earnings outlook, analysts said.
Textile issue Victor Onward fell HK$0.10 to HK$1.63, the day's worst performer. Brokers provided no reason for the counter's decline.
Television tube maker Baoshi shed HK$0.02 to HK$2.55 on the session's most active trade of 4.04 million shares. The issue had gained rather heavily early last week, an analyst noted.

Guangdong Electric Power inched down HK$0.01 to HK$5.39. The A share market gained on Thursday due to an official report on the State Council's plan to further tighten controls on the country's commodities futures market, brokers said.

The Shenzhen-based Securities Times quoted the Securities Commission of the State Council as saying that it would further strengthen its supervision over futures trading and not approve the setting up of new futures brokerages.
The A share index rose 5.40 points, or 1.91 percent, to end at 288.31, with turnover expanding to 6.77 billion yuan from 6.06 billion yuan last Friday.
The composite index ended up 4.83 points, or 1.81 percent, at 271.61.
Sichuan Tiange was the focus of demand by institutional punters, brokers said. The garment maker surged 1.83 yuan, or 35.12 percent, to 7.04 yuan.
Newcomer Gujing Distillery caught the brunt of profit-taking, brokers said. The issue slid 1.12 yuan, or 4.87 percent, to 21.88 yuan.
